title: Aldergrove & Vale property set: neutralize eight mixed-light room shots to an in-frame grey card, author one bright-and-airy house look, pull the blown windows, then data-merge a press-ready listing brochure
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork high-volume real-estate photo-editing open call (an agency's go-to editor receives room-by-room listing captures; the named edit list is 'window pulls, sky replacement, color correction, vertical/horizontal alignment, lawn enhancement, lens distortion correction, general cleanup'; deliverable = 'high-quality, portal-ready images with consistent style across each property'; '20-40 photos per listing', '24-48h turnaround'). The real post named no client, so the brand is laundered to a FICTIONAL brokerage, Aldergrove & Vale Realty, and a fictional listing, 14 Marlowe Crescent; no real company, person, product, marketplace, or listing-service trademark is named (the generic 'listing portal / property brochure' replaces any branded listing-service name). The vague open call is fixed into a runnable, gradeable batch: ONE representative listing shot as EIGHT frames — a wide-dynamic-range exterior hero plus six interiors and a back-garden exterior — each captured under the room's own mixed light (cool north-window living room, warm-tungsten kitchen, split lamp+window bedroom, cool-LED bathroom, a genuinely warm walnut study under near-neutral light, a dim underexposed dining room, an overexposed sunlit patio), with a neutral 18% grey balance card set in the corner of every frame so 'consistent style across the property' becomes a MEASURABLE neutralisation target rather than an eyeball claim. HONEST CAPABILITY SUBSTITUTIONS forced by the connector surface: (1) there is no HDR bracket-MERGE tool, so the client supplies one wide-DR frame per room and tone is recovered via authored highlight/shadow/exposure primitives — the single-file equivalent of a bracket blend; (2) literal 'sky replacement' is background-replace-by-prompt and is NOT available, so the exterior sky is delivered as a MASKED sky ENHANCEMENT (select the sky, recover highlights, deepen the existing blue within band) — never a swap, flagged as the portal-safe version; (3) 'general cleanup' is scoped to tonal/geometry only (straighten, crop, WB), never AI object removal; (4) 'lens distortion / vertical alignment' is auto-straighten + crop-to-bounds. The consistent house look is AUTHORED from image_apply_adjustments primitives (not a preset, not auto-tone). The owned endpoint is a genuine hand-authored single-record InDesign brochure template merged one-record-per-page, so the property brochure is a real data-merge, never a converted PDF and never a multi-up grid. No generative fill/expand, no compositing, no upscaling, no from-scratch art.
one_line_ask: Take eight room shots of one listing photographed under different mixed lighting (each with a grey reference card in frame), neutralise and grade every one to one consistent bright-and-airy Aldergrove & Vale house look measured against the card, pull the blown windows and enhance the exterior sky and lawn, reframe the exterior into a web hero, vectorize the agency wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored single-record brochure template against the room roster into one press-ready property brochure, one page per room.
full_brief:
Aldergrove & Vale Realty is listing 14 Marlowe Crescent and needs the photo set turned into portal-ready images plus a press-ready property brochure. We shot the whole house in one pass — every room under whatever light it had, plus the front and back exteriors — so straight out of the folder the frames do not match: some rooms read warm, some cool, some are dim, at least one bright window blows out, and on the exterior the big front windows and the sky are hot over a shaded facade. Because we knew the light was uneven room to room, we set a neutral 18% grey balance card in the corner of every single frame.

What we need first is one deliberately-designed, CONSISTENT 'bright & airy' house look across the whole set — not eight mismatched snapshots. Use the grey card in each frame as your ground truth: neutralise every frame so its card reads truly neutral (no residual warm, cool or green cast) and so all eight settle on ONE shared white point, then carry ONE restrained house tone across the set — clean, bright, a touch warm in the highlights, gentle contrast and clarity — so the rooms feel like one home. Do NOT force a single blanket correction across the batch: each room was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target, and some rooms are genuinely warm by design, so read each card rather than assuming a cast and cooling it. When you are done, hand us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm they were matched to the card, not eyeballed.

On the exterior hero the verticals are leaning and the horizon is off — level it and crop to clean bounds (that is our alignment / lens cleanup). The big front windows and the sky are blown: pull them back so the glass shows structure instead of glare, and enhance the existing sky so it reads as a deep, believable blue — we are NOT swapping in a new sky, just recovering and deepening the one that is there, which keeps it portal-safe. Lift the front lawn so it looks healthy and inviting. Wherever an interior has a blown-out window, recover it the same way so the room feels open, not washed out.

Then build the deliverables: (1) the exterior hero as a wide 16:9 web hero, graded and reframed with clean space to one side for an overlaid headline; (2) a press-ready US Letter property brochure — ONE page per room, each page carrying that room's name, dimensions and a short feature caption bound verbatim from the roster we give you, its matching graded photo dropped in, and our agency wordmark crisp in the masthead — page one is the exterior hero. Our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white stock; get it clean and razor-sharp as a vector for the masthead so it does not print fuzzy. Bind our roster copy verbatim — do not rewrite room names, dimensions or captions.

Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point while genuinely-warm rooms keep their real color; blown windows recovered and the exterior sky and lawn enhanced (not replaced); the brochure exactly one page per room at ~300 DPI US Letter; the wordmark a crisp vector in every masthead; and a short per-frame parameter sheet so 'matched' is verifiable.

inputs.name: raw_exterior_front_hero.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a two-story suburban home front elevation, single wide-dynamic-range exposure: the brick-and-siding facade sits in open shade and reads slightly underexposed while the sky is bright and near-blown and the large front windows are blown out to white glare, a green-but-slightly-patchy front lawn and paved driveway in foreground, leaning vertical lines and a horizon tilted ~4 degrees as if shot handheld and not leveled, slight lens barrel distortion at the edges. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a small white patch is propped on the driveway at the lower-left frame edge, clearly visible. Real brick and window-reflection texture, midday overcast-bright light, no people, no text, no watermark, un-retouched documentary HDR-source look, NOT tone-mapped, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: The HERO and the frame that carries the most craft: leaning verticals + ~4deg tilt (auto_straighten/crop have real work), blown front windows (the window pull must mask them and recover highlight/white detail so the glass shows structure), a bright near-blown sky (masked sky ENHANCEMENT — recover highlights + deepen blue in-band, NOT a replacement), and a patchy lawn (masked green lift). The grey card sits FAR lower-left so it can be neutralised first and cropped OUT when the plate is reframed for the 16:9 hero and for the brochure. Real-camera scale (~4400 px) so every crop is downscale-only to fill the brochure frame at ~300 DPI. The exterior's own cast is a cool overcast, so its corrective differs from the interiors.

inputs.name: raw_living_room_northwindow.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a staged living room with a large window wall on one side that is very bright and near-blown showing only white outside, cool north-facing daylight, neutral sofa, coffee table, hardwood floor, a distinctly COOL/blue and slightly flat unedited white balance. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a white patch rests on the coffee table in view. No people, no text, no watermark, realistic shadows and material texture, shot wide-angle, un-retouched documentary look, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Interior with a COOL cast + a blown window: needs WARMING to neutralise its grey card (the OPPOSITE direction to the warm kitchen frame, so one shared white-balance across the batch cannot serve both — the identical-params trap), AND a masked window pull to recover the blown glass. Grey card on the table is the target; card is cropped out of the delivered brochure frame.

inputs.name: raw_kitchen_tungsten.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a staged modern kitchen, white cabinets, stone countertop, stainless appliances, lit by warm under-cabinet and ceiling TUNGSTEN, with a window over the sink that is bright and slightly blown to daylight. Strongly WARM/amber unedited white balance, normal exposure. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a white patch sits on the countertop in view. No people, no text, no watermark, realistic reflections and texture, wide-angle, un-retouched, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Interior with a WARM tungsten cast + a slightly blown window: must move the OPPOSITE way from the cool living room — COOL the white balance to neutralise its card — and take a masked window pull on the over-sink window. Two interiors that look superficially similar (both 'a room with a bright window') but take opposite corrections: getting the direction wrong is invisible until the set is viewed together.

inputs.name: raw_primary_bedroom_mixed.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a staged primary bedroom lit by a MIX of a warm bedside lamp on one side and cool window light on the other, so the cast is split and uneven across the room, upholstered bed, neutral linens, normal exposure and flat contrast. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a white patch is propped on the nightstand in view. No people, no text, no watermark, realistic texture, wide-angle, un-retouched, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Split warm/cool cast — the hardest to neutralise to the card; the agent must average toward the card's neutral rather than fully killing one side, and drive the card grey neutral even if one wall stays a touch warmer. Distinct correction from every other frame. No blown window here (no window pull needed — deciding that is part of the job).

inputs.name: raw_bathroom_led.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a staged bathroom lit by overhead cool LED / fluorescent fixtures, white vanity, tile, mirror, with a distinct GREEN/magenta-deficient cool cast and normal exposure. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a white patch rests on the vanity in view. No people, no text, no watermark, realistic tile and chrome texture, wide-angle, un-retouched, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Green LED/fluorescent cast needs a TINT (green->magenta) correction, a different axis from the warm/cool temperature frames — a temperature-only fix leaves a green card and fails the gate. Forces per-frame reasoning rather than one slider. No blown window.

inputs.name: raw_study_walnut.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a staged home study with walnut wall panelling, a wood desk and leather chair, warm bookshelf tones, shot under near-neutral balanced daylight so the room's warmth is the real wood color, NOT a lighting cast — the scene reads genuinely warm and rich but is correctly exposed and correctly balanced. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a white patch sits on the desk in view and already reads close to neutral. No people, no text, no watermark, realistic wood grain and leather texture, wide-angle, un-retouched, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. The study looks warm, but that warmth is genuine walnut/leather color and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set and lay the shared house tone). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'cool the warm cast' correction it used on the kitchen, or 'cools an imagined amber cast', will neutralise the card off-neutral and strip the walnut color the listing is selling. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. No blown window.

inputs.name: raw_dining_room_dim.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a staged dining room, table and chairs, sideboard, lit dimly by a single fixture with the blinds mostly drawn, clearly UNDEREXPOSED and flat with muddy shadows and a mildly warm cast. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a white patch rests on the dining table in view. No people, no text, no watermark, realistic texture, wide-angle, un-retouched, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Dim/underexposed: the dominant move is TONAL — lift exposure and open the shadows with added contrast/clarity — then neutralise the mild warm cast to the card. A different problem from the cool/warm/green frames; the WB move is small, the exposure move is large. Its grey card still must land on the shared white point and brightness.

inputs.name: raw_back_patio_sun.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Real full-frame camera capture (~4400x2933 px, 3:2) of a back garden patio with outdoor furniture, lawn and fence, shot in strong late-afternoon SUN so it is clearly OVEREXPOSED and warm, with near-blown highlights on the paving and a hazy bright sky. A neutral 18% grey balance card with a white patch is propped on the patio table in view. No people, no text, no watermark, realistic paving and foliage texture, wide-angle, un-retouched, NOT CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: The back exterior: OVEREXPOSED and warm — must PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown paving and COOL slightly to neutralise its card, the opposite tonal AND WB direction from the dim dining room. Proves the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Grey card on the table is the target; card cropped out of the brochure frame.

inputs.name: aldergrove_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Aldergrove & Vale Realty' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: an elegant thin serif, deep charcoal lettering with a small crest glyph, rendered as a real scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around the mark, and edges are a touch soft. High contrast so that, once cleaned, it vectorizes cleanly. No photographic gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2deg rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper field and bake in the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/contrast to separate ink from ground, crop to the mark's bounds, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. Delivered onto every brochure masthead via a second @-image merge column, never free-form placement.

inputs.name: marlowe_crescent_brochure_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait property-brochure page — ONE room per page. It must carry live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<room_name>>, <<dimensions>>, <<feature_caption>>, <<listing_line>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a large room-photo frame bound to @image (the matching graded room photo) and a masthead frame at the top bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized agency wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-room grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one room's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record brochure page is the correct, connector-doable shape; a converted-PDF template with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@image, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves the row's graded room photo AND the shared vectorized wordmark per page, giving the chain-produced wordmark a real connector-doable path onto every masthead without any free-form placement. Supplied as an input, not a chain output.

inputs.name: marlowe_crescent_room_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns room_name,dimensions,feature_caption,listing_line,@image,@Wordmark holding 8 rows, one per room of 14 Marlowe Crescent, in this page order: Front Exterior, Living Room, Kitchen, Primary Bedroom, Bathroom, Study, Dining Room, Back Garden. Each row carries a short factual room name, a dimensions string (e.g. '4.8m x 3.9m'), a one-line feature caption (e.g. 'South-facing bay windows and original oak flooring'), and a listing_line (address / price band, identical across rows, e.g. '14 Marlowe Crescent — offers over $000,000'). The @image column names that room's matching prepped graded photo file (e.g. @living_room_graded.jpg) so the one-file-per-row merge drops each graded photo into that page's room frame. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @aldergrove_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every page as a merge bind. Column names must exactly match the template fields <<room_name>>,<<dimensions>>,<<feature_caption>>,<<listing_line>> and the two @image-path columns @image and @Wordmark. Front Exterior is row 1 so the exterior hero is page 1 of the merged brochure.
inputs.realism_notes: Headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row merge binds copy, the correct room photo, AND the shared wordmark per page. @Wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all eight rows. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight brochure pages (page-count = row-count gate). Copy is bound verbatim; no room-name/dimension/caption is rewritten by the agent. CSV content carries no per-frame lighting diagnosis — only listing copy.

outputs.name: marlowe_crescent_property_brochure.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait brochure pages — ONE room per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8, page 1 = Front Exterior hero) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each page binds its room_name/dimensions/feature_caption/listing_line verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralised graded photo dropped into the room image frame (via @image) and the crisp vectorized agency wordmark dropped into the masthead frame (via @Wordmark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality.

outputs.name: graded_room_set_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralised, straightened, house-look-graded room frames, delivered as the brochure-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralised masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralised master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within ~3 levels) with the whole set matched to one shared white point within ~4 levels, while the genuinely-warm study keeps its real walnut color (its card also neutral); one shared bright-and-airy house tone (warm-highlight / clean-neutral, modest contrast + clarity + gentle vibrance) is present across all eight; (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered brochure crop (the *_graded output that binds into that room's page) — framed on the room with the grey card fully cropped OUT. The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Blown windows on the frames that carry them are recovered (glass shows structure). Accompanied by the per-frame parameter report.

outputs.name: exterior_hero_web_16x9.png
outputs.spec: The Front Exterior graded master (straightened, window-pulled, sky-enhanced, lawn-lifted, neutralised, house-look) reframed by an honest off-center crop of the native 3:2 to a wide 16:9 web hero (~2880x1620) with the house offset to one side so the other side gives the web team clean negative space for an overlaid headline; grey card cropped out; downscale-only from the ~4400px source, no upscale, no canvas extend; sRGB PNG.

outputs.name: aldergrove_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the agency wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark's bounds, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured off-white paper ground and no residual skew. This SVG is what @Wordmark binds into every brochure masthead.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short accompanying note (secondary to the images, NOT the primary deliverable) in which the agent reports, per room frame: the corrective white-balance move made to hit the card (temperature and tint direction/magnitude), the exposure delta, and — for the frames that carry a blown window — that a masked window pull was applied. Plus a one-line confirmation that each frame's grey card reads neutral and lands on the common white point, and that the set shares one bright-and-airy house tone. This makes 'matched to the card' verifiable rather than asserted; the corrections must be non-identical across the warm, cool, green, split, dim, and overexposed frames.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: raw_exterior_front_hero.jpg, raw_living_room_northwindow.jpg, raw_kitchen_tungsten.jpg, raw_primary_bedroom_mixed.jpg, raw_bathroom_led.jpg, raw_study_walnut.jpg, raw_dining_room_dim.jpg, raw_back_patio_sun.jpg, aldergrove_wordmark_scan.png
connector_workflow.note: Ingest the eight client room captures plus the wordmark scan into the working project in one load so every downstream edit runs against real asset references. Plumbing, not difficulty.

Level the leaning verticals / tilted horizon on the exterior hero before any grading or reframing, so the later off-center crop is measured against a true horizon. The alignment / lens-cleanup deliverable. Consumes the uploaded exterior.

ESTABLISH the shared bright-and-airy house look on the exterior and record it as the target the other frames must hit. Using this frame's in-frame grey card as reference, dial temperature and tint to drive that card to true neutral, set exposure/highlights/shadows so the shaded facade opens and the card sits at the common brightness, then author the house tone with primitives: warm-highlight / clean-neutral balance, modest contrast and clarity, gentle vibrance. Reason the correction from THIS card — do not assume a cast. This is an authored grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone; report the temp/tint/exposure chosen (they define the common target). Consumes step 2.

Semantically select the bright front window glass ('the blown-out front windows of the house') for the window pull. Names a real object, so select_by_prompt applies; returns a maskURI. Not a hue or geometric-band selection.

WINDOW PULL (masked): inside the window mask, pull highlights and whites down and add a touch of clarity so the glass recovers structure instead of glaring. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local recovery confined to the glass and does not darken the rest of the facade. Consumes step 3 image + step 4 mask.
Semantically select the sky above the roofline for the portal-safe sky ENHANCEMENT (not a replacement — replacement is generative and unavailable). Real-object selection; returns a maskURI.

Masked sky enhancement: within the sky mask deepen and enrich the existing blue by lifting the blue band's saturation and settling its luminance — a moderate IN-BAND move (no near-complementary rotation) that recovers a believable sky, never a swap. image_adjust_hsl is the only masked recolor path. Consumes step 5 image + step 6 mask.
Semantically select the front lawn grass for the lawn enhancement. Real-object selection; returns a maskURI.

Masked lawn enhancement: within the lawn mask lift the green band's saturation and luminance so the grass reads healthy and inviting, in-band (no hue jump). Produces the finished exterior graded master (grey card still in frame) — retained for neutrality grading and feeding both the web hero and the brochure crop. Consumes step 7 image + step 8 mask.

Crop the exterior graded master to the brochure room frame, framing on the house with the grey card cropped OUT — this crop (card removed) binds into page 1 (@image). The pre-crop master (exterior_graded, card still in frame) is retained as the neutrality-grading artifact. Downscale/reframe of existing pixels only; onSubjectClipping='extract'; never canvas-extend or upscale.

Honest off-center reframe of the ~4400px exterior graded master to a 16:9 ~2880x1620 web hero: crop with the house offset to one side so the other side becomes clean headline negative space, cropping the grey card OUT in the same move. Downscale-only from the camera-scale source; no upscale, no canvas extend. DELIVERABLE exterior_hero_web_16x9.png.

Neutralise the living room to its in-frame grey card and land it on the shared white point set in step 3, then lay the same shared house tone. Reason THIS frame's own white-balance and exposure correction from its card — do not copy another frame's numbers. Authored primitives, no preset/auto-tone. Report the move. Retained master (card in frame). Consumes the uploaded living room.

Semantically select the bright window glass in the living room for a window pull, since this room's window is blown. Real-object selection; returns a maskURI. (Whether a frame needs this is a per-frame decision.)

Masked window pull: recover highlights/whites inside the window mask so the glass reads open, not washed out, without darkening the room. Produces the living room graded master. Consumes step 12 image + step 13 mask.
Crop the living room graded master to the brochure room frame, grey card cropped OUT (binds via @image); pre-crop master retained for neutrality grading. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Neutralise the kitchen to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and lay the shared house tone. Reason this frame's own correction from its card — its light differs from the living room, so its move must differ. Report the move. Retained master (card in frame). Consumes the uploaded kitchen.
Semantically select the bright over-sink window glass for a window pull. Real-object selection; returns a maskURI.
Masked window pull: recover the blown over-sink window inside its mask so it reads daylight-open. Produces the kitchen graded master. Consumes step 16 image + step 17 mask.
Crop the kitchen graded master to the brochure room frame, grey card cropped OUT (binds via @image); pre-crop master retained. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Neutralise the primary bedroom to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and lay the shared house tone. Its light differs again, so reason its own white-balance and exposure move from its card and drive the card grey neutral even where the room light is uneven. Report the move. Retained master. Consumes the uploaded bedroom.

Crop the bedroom graded master to the brochure room frame, grey card cropped OUT (binds via @image); pre-crop master retained. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. No window pull applied to this frame — deciding it does not need one is part of the job.

Neutralise the bathroom to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and lay the shared house tone. This frame's cast is on a different axis, so the correction that lands its card neutral is not the same kind of move as the temperature frames. Report the move. Retained master. Consumes the uploaded bathroom.
Crop the bathroom graded master to the brochure room frame, grey card cropped OUT (binds via @image); pre-crop master retained. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Neutralise the study to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and lay the shared house tone. Read THIS card: where the card already reads neutral, hold white balance and only match brightness — do not chase a cast that the card says is not there, or the room's genuine material color is stripped. Match exposure/tone to the set. Report the move (including that WB was held if the card is already neutral). Retained master. Consumes the uploaded study.
Crop the study graded master to the brochure room frame, grey card cropped OUT (binds via @image); pre-crop master retained. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Neutralise the dining room to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and lay the shared house tone. Here the dominant correction is tonal — open the frame to the common brightness and contrast — with the white-balance move to the card kept measured. Report the move. Retained master. Consumes the uploaded dining room.
Crop the dining graded master to the brochure room frame, grey card cropped OUT (binds via @image); pre-crop master retained. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Neutralise the back patio to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and lay the shared house tone. Recover the bright paving to the common brightness and neutralise the card — the opposite tonal direction from the dim dining room. Report the move. Retained master. Consumes the uploaded patio.

Crop the patio graded master to the brochure room frame, grey card cropped OUT (binds via @image); pre-crop master retained. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. All eight frames now share one white point and one house tone, each neutralised to its own grey card.

Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits ~2deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation. Consumes the uploaded wordmark scan.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward white so the charcoal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges. Consumes step 30.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field. Consumes step 31.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). Consumes step 32.

Vectorize the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. DELIVERABLE aldergrove_wordmark.svg. Consumes step 33.
